data.hypothesis: Row-wise sorted obstacle intervals reduce blocked-grid storage and per-cell obstacle checks. On AArch64, a four-lane prefix scan can evaluate each open interval while explicitly carrying the true horizontal DP dependency, potentially speeding the row recurrence without an invalid SIMD directive.
data.notes: The recurrence still requires a carry between SIMD chunks and rows; blocked cells reset it. The SIMD path reduces after each addition stage to keep signed 32-bit lanes in range, with scalar tails and a portable scalar fallback. The algorithm remains O(N^2) in work; storage is O(N+M).
transformations: Replace the N-by-N blocked-cell bitmap with per-row sorted, deduplicated blocked-column lists and process each row as open intervals.
Use two O(N) DP rows and swap them after each row instead of copying the completed row.
On AArch64, compute four-cell inclusive prefix sums with NEON lane shifts, modulo reduction, and a carried final lane; retain scalar tails and a scalar fallback on other architectures.
